sourceDiscrepancies.lateral-thoracic-breathing: Page 12 lists a breath-holding progression but also says to avoid holding the breath. The teaching cue follows the smooth, continuous breathing instruction; the conflicting progression is omitted below.
sourceDiscrepancies.cleopatra: Pages 20 and 65 show and describe standing arm opening, but their watch points describe side support and lateral flexion. Instructor review is required to reconcile those sections.
sourceDiscrepancies.squat: Page 21 repeats shoulder-roll muscles and watch points. Use its squat setup, movement, purpose and lower table; the inconsistent muscle list and main watch points are omitted.
sourceDiscrepancies.roll-down-supine: Page 27 calls this Roll Down Variation (supine); the classical table calls the related exercise Roll-Up. The photographs show a bent-knee preparation, while the written full version uses straight legs. This is distinct from the retired standing Roll Down.
sourceDiscrepancies.roll-over: Page 4 marks Roll-Over amber, but the Unit 2 overview on page 22 lists it among red exercises. Instructor review is required.
sourceDiscrepancies.jackknife: Page 6 marks Jackknife amber, but page 32 lists it among red exercises. Instructor review is required.
sourceDiscrepancies.high-scissors: Page 5 marks the classical exercise red; page 39 says it is not red because its preparations are widely used. The full inversion remains Advanced and requires instructor review; supine preparations are not the same exercise.
sourceDiscrepancies.high-bicycle: Page 5 marks the classical exercise red; page 40 says it is not red because its preparations are widely used. The full inversion remains Advanced and requires instructor review; supine preparations are not the same exercise.
sourceDiscrepancies.single-leg-extension: Page 35 calls the illustrated exercise a beginner variation, but its setup lifts both legs into tabletop with the head and shoulders raised. This full card uses Intermediate; head-down and foot-supported preparations remain in the source regressions.
sourceDiscrepancies.one-leg-kick: Page 47 lists Rocking variations under One Leg Kick. Those mismatched variations are omitted; its One Leg Kick setup and movement are retained.
sourceDiscrepancies.double-leg-kick: Page 48 describes an arm reach behind the body, while the photographs retain forearm support. The image illustrates the supported variation; confirm the intended variation when teaching.
sourceDiscrepancies.push-up: Page 55 says to articulate the spine in its watch points, but its movement says to lower in one line. The cue follows the latter and the conflicting watch point is omitted.
sourceDiscrepancies.upper-body-reaches: Page 67 says shoulder adduction while describing an overhead reach. The cue uses the pictured reach without assigning that conflicting anatomical term.
sourceDiscrepancies.90-90-lunge: Page 72 describes a kneeling start and tall-kneeling finish, but shows a standing split squat. Instructor review is required before using this card.
sourceDiscrepancies.spinal-twist-supine: Page 78 gives inhale to lower and exhale to return in Movement & Breath, but says exhale during twist in its lower watch-point table. The cue follows Movement & Breath.
sourceDiscrepancies.dumbwaiter: The lower table on pages 19 and 64 includes seated spinal-twist preparations that do not match the standing arm exercise. The teaching cue follows the standing setup and movement; confirm those table entries before using them.

timing: 75 seconds is the existing app planning block, not a duration prescribed by the manual.
migration: Retire untouched old bundled IDs from the active library. Preserve instructor-edited samples, custom entries, deleted IDs, saved plans and teaching history. New manual IDs do not reinterpret historical cards.
sourceText: Original spelling retained. Broken table-font punctuation normalised to hyphens; explicitly identified contradictory passages omitted as described per movement.

countAudit.method: Count dedicated exercise headings once, merge Dumbwaiter and Cleopatra repeats, then add four names-only examples from page 74. Classical repertoire tables, series overviews, preparations, progressions and variations are not additional standalone entries.
countAudit.overviewAliases: Roll-Up maps to the supine Roll Down card; Lunge With Skater maps to Skater; Leg Abduction in the standing overview is covered by the existing leg-abduction card and its standing preparation.
